title: Synthesis of current relative-humidity references for classrooms, combining ABNT NBR 17037:2023, ABNT NBR 16401-2:2024, ANSI/ASHRAE 55-2023, EPA school moisture guidance, and historical ANVISA RE 9/2003 revoked by RDC 886/2024
author_or_body: ABNT; ANVISA; ASHRAE; U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
edition_year: ABNT NBR 17037:2023 with correction history visible in 2024 secondary previews [uncertain]; ABNT NBR 16401-2:2024 published on 2024-11-19; ANSI/ASHRAE 55-2023 current as of 2026-08-24; EPA school moisture guidance current as accessed on 2026-08-24; ANVISA RE 9/2003 revoked by RDC 886/2024
source_type: Current technical standards and official agency guidance, plus one historical revoked regulation used only for traceability
normative_status: Current IAQ reference for artificially conditioned non-residential spaces: ABNT NBR 17037:2023. Current thermal-comfort references: ABNT NBR 16401-2:2024 and ANSI/ASHRAE 55-2023. Historical only: ANVISA RE 9/2003, expressly revoked by RDC 886/2024.
source_hierarchy: Highest weight: official regulatory status pages and official standard catalog status pages. Medium weight: official EPA school moisture guidance. Lower weight: public secondary previews used only to inspect paywalled ABNT clause content.
country_or_jurisdiction: Brazil for ABNT and ANVISA applicability; international for ASHRAE thermal-comfort method; U.S. EPA used only as non-Brazilian operational school moisture guidance
environment_type: University classroom or similar non-residential occupied room, especially if artificially conditioned
occupant_profile: Adult students and instructors; general healthy occupants performing sedentary or light activity
room_operation_mode: Natural ventilation, mixed mode, or artificial air conditioning may occur depending on the classroom and date [uncertain]
operating_context: Night classes in an occupied classroom, with possible variation in windows, fans, air conditioning, blinds, and weather exposure across sessions [uncertain]
excluded_conditions: Do not use relative humidity alone to claim thermal comfort, health protection, learning impact, or full regulatory compliance. The ABNT NBR 17037 humidity band applies to artificially conditioned non-residential environments. EPA school guidance is operational guidance, not Brazilian compliance text. Revoked RE 9/2003 must not be treated as a current legal limit.
limit_or_range: Current Brazilian IAQ reference for artificially conditioned non-residential spaces: 35% to 65% RH from ABNT NBR 17037:2023, publicly verified through secondary preview of a paywalled standard [uncertain]. Current thermal-comfort standards do not provide a stand-alone RH comfort compliance band; instead they require multi-variable assessment such as PMV/PPD or other full comfort methods. Operational school moisture guidance: keep RH below 60%, ideally between 30% and 50%. Historical traceability only: revoked ANVISA RE 9/2003 used 40% to 65% in summer and 35% to 65% in winter.
meaning_of_parameter: Indoor-air-quality screening in conditioned rooms, moisture and mold attention screening, and one input variable in thermal-comfort assessment; not a sufficient comfort criterion by itself
spatial_reference_zone: Occupied zone. For ABNT NBR 17037 secondary public preview, this zone is described between the floor and 1.80 m, more than 0.3 m from internal walls and more than 1.0 m from external walls, windows, and HVAC components [uncertain].
measurement_position: A single node should be placed within the occupied zone at representative seated or breathing height and away from direct solar gain, supply diffusers, exterior openings, and localized moisture sources; final deployment coordinates are still project-specific [uncertain]
sensor_orientation: No special orientation is normally required for capacitive RH sensing, but the sensor should be exposed to room air and protected from blocked airflow, direct discharge, radiant heating, and enclosure self-heating
spatial_representativeness: Point measurement only; it represents local air at the sensor and cannot prove uniformity or whole-room compliance
unmeasured_relevant_variables: Air temperature, mean radiant temperature, air speed, clothing, metabolic rate, occupancy density, outdoor conditions, outdoor air flow, moisture sources, condensation, and HVAC control state
instrument_specification: Low-cost digital thermo-hygrometer integrated in the prototype, using the manufacturer-stated range, resolution, and accuracy for the chosen sensor model; exact final sensor model and verified specification are not fixed in this item [uncertain]
calibration_status: The alert logic should only be trusted after comparison against a traceable thermo-hygrometer or at least a field comparison with a calibrated reference; the currently available reference instrument is not confirmed [uncertain]
response_time: Use the installed sensor datasheet response time and allow for enclosure and airflow stabilization; the exact value for the chosen hardware is not fixed here [uncertain]
sensor_hysteresis_and_drift: Capacitive RH sensors commonly exhibit hysteresis and long-term drift, so near-threshold values need tolerance bands and periodic checks; the magnitude for the chosen device is not yet verified [uncertain]
sampling_interval: Use the prototype acquisition interval; a 1 min to 5 min interval is generally adequate for classroom screening, but the project-final interval is still a design choice [uncertain]
valid_data_requirement: A rolling window should be treated as valid only when most expected samples are present and the sensor status is normal; 80% valid samples per window is a defensible engineering rule, not a normative one [uncertain]
gap_and_outlier_handling: Flag missing, frozen, or physically implausible RH values; ignore obvious transients from startup, cleaning, direct breath plumes, or temporary local interference; do not bridge long gaps when deciding alert state
aggregation_window: Prefer a rolling 15 min to 30 min mean or median for dashboard state instead of instantaneous RH, but the final window is an engineering decision rather than a normative requirement [uncertain]
trigger_rule: Suggested engineering screening for an artificially conditioned classroom: set Attention when RH stays outside 35% to 65% for at least 15 min, and set Alert when RH stays below 30% or above 65% for at least 30 min, or remains above 60% persistently when the focus is school moisture control. This is an engineering triage rule, not direct comfort compliance [uncertain].
clear_rule: Clear only after RH returns to the acceptable band with hysteresis, for example clearing Attention after 15 min back inside 37% to 63%, and clearing Alert only after sustained return below 60% for high-humidity events or above 32% for low-humidity events [uncertain]
rule_basis: Normative basis for conditioned-space IAQ screening: ABNT NBR 17037:2023. Comfort basis: ABNT NBR 16401-2:2024 and ANSI/ASHRAE 55-2023 require multi-variable thermal assessment, so any RH-only alert is an internal engineering triage rule. Building moisture basis: EPA school guidance to keep RH below 60%, ideally 30% to 50%. Historical traceability only: ANVISA RE 9/2003, revoked by RDC 886/2024.
dashboard_message: Relative humidity is within the configured screening band, outside the conditioned-space screening band, persistently high for moisture attention, or persistently low for dryness attention. This is a screening indicator only, not proof of comfort or legal noncompliance.
possible_management_investigation: Check whether windows, doors, fans, AC operation, occupancy density, cleaning or wet activities, rain intrusion, condensate drainage, or local sensor placement explain the reading
interpretation_limits: Relative humidity alone cannot diagnose mold, ventilation adequacy, infection risk, sick-building effects, learning impact, or comfort acceptance. A single sensor cannot separate room-wide conditions from a local microclimate.
overinterpretation_risk: Users may mistake a humidity alert for a legal violation or a direct health diagnosis, and may incorrectly assume normal RH proves full IAQ or thermal comfort
project_requirement: Support a low-cost classroom dashboard that separates current normative references from historical or operational guidance and avoids unsupported compliance claims
destination_in_text: Methodology chapter for alert logic, results discussion for humidity behavior, and limitations section on what the dashboard can and cannot infer
verification_state: Partially verified. Public primary sources confirm the revocation of RE 9/2003 by RDC 886/2024, the current status of ANSI/ASHRAE 55-2023, the publication status of ISO 7730:2025, EPA school moisture guidance, and the current publication status of ABNT NBR 17037 and ABNT NBR 16401-2. Exact ABNT clause wording used here was publicly checked mainly through secondary previews because the standards are paywalled [uncertain].
